content: Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. For guidance on disposal, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. The information provided here was last updated in September 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Stelara Uses: Ustekinumab is prescribed to treat plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and certain bowel conditions such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. It works by inhibiting specific natural proteins in the body, interleukin-12 and interleukin-23, which are responsible for causing inflammation in these conditions. While ustekinumab does not cure these diseases, it helps reduce their symptoms. How to Use: Before starting ustekinumab, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Review these materials each time you receive a refill. Consult your healthcare provider for instructions on how to prepare and administer this medication. Prior to initiating treatment, you should undergo a tuberculosis (TB) skin test to check for latent TB, a type of tuberculosis that may not present symptoms. Ustekinumab is administered as an injection under the skin, as directed by your doctor. For psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis, the first two doses are typically given four weeks apart, followed by maintenance doses every 12 weeks. For Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, the initial dose is usually administered intravenously by a healthcare professional, followed by subcutaneous injections every eight weeks. When injecting under the skin, the medication can be administered in the upper arms, buttocks, thighs, or abdomen. Do not shake the medication. The product may contain a few small white particles, which is normal. However, if you notice discoloration or other particles, do not use the liquid. Before each injection, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. Avoid injecting into irritated, sore, or infected skin. To reduce bruising, refrain from rubbing the injection site after administration. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Side Effects: Common side effects include bruising, itching, pain, redness, swelling, or hardening of the skin at the injection site. These reactions typically resolve within one to two days. Other possible side effects include headache, back pain, or sinus/throat pain. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Ustekinumab can affect your immune system, potentially lowering your body's ability to fight infections. This may increase your risk of serious infections, such as lung infections, bone/joint infections, skin infections, sinus infections, or bowel/gallbladder infections. It may also make it harder to combat existing infections. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience signs of infection, such as persistent nausea or vomiting, worsening redness/swelling/tenderness at the injection site after two days, fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, painful or frequent urination, unusual vaginal discharge or burning/itching/odor, or severe stomach pain. In rare cases, ustekinumab may cause a potentially fatal condition called posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Additionally, there is a rare risk of developing cancer, including skin cancer, with this medication. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using ustekinumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex in the needle cover of the prefilled syringe, which could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ustekinumab may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid receiving immunizations or vaccinations without your doctor's approval. Stay away from individuals who have recently received live vaccines, such as the oral polio vaccine or nasal flu vaccine. Avoid receiving BCG vaccines for one year after completing ustekinumab treatment. Additionally, avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Ustekinumab may pass into breast milk; consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring and Appointments: While using this medication, regular lab and medical tests, such as skin exams, may be required. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Missed Dose: It is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized guidance.
